text:
harper: Quick docs snag on POST /v1/uploads response shape. The API ref (current PR) documents the response as:
```json
{
  "id": 12345,
  "url": "https://cdn.redwood.ai/.../pic.png",
  "mime_type": "image/png"
}
```
but the actual hosted runtime returns this shape today:
```json
{
  "id": "upload_01G...",
  "object_key": "uploads/customer123/pic.png",
  "content_type": "image/png",
  "size_bytes": 23456
}
```
harper: That mismatch caused an SDK test failure — our JS SDK expects numeric id and `url` field to build presigned URLs.

wayne: Oof. Looks like two independent mismatches: `id` type + name, and `url` vs `object_key`/presign pattern, and the content-type field naming. We should sync the API ref with runtime (prefer string id, object_key, content_type, size_bytes).

elaine: Agreed. Proposed doc fixes: update response schema in OpenAPI to show string id, object_key, content_type, size_bytes, and add an examples block showing the presign flow (server returns object_key + client calls /presign or SDK helper). Also add a migration note for customers relying on numeric ids or `url` field.

sanjay: Confirming runtime: hosted returns string ids (prefix upload_), stores object_key instead of returning a direct CDN URL — customers should use our presign endpoint or SDK convenience method to get a URL. Dedicated/private older installs may have returned `url` directly; that's why some references differ. We'll call out that behaviour explicitly.

harper: Can we also add a short compatibility table in the ref: field name | hosted (current) | legacy dedicated | notes? That would be helpful for SEs.

wayne: Good idea. I'll update the OpenAPI response schema and add two example responses (hosted + legacy-dedicated). I'll also update the examples in the SDK snippets section so the JS snippet uses client.getUploadUrl(upload.object_key) instead of reading url directly.

elaine: Small docs nit: update the API examples that parse id to treat it as string in code snippets (JS + Python). Some of the test snippets do math on id which will break.

harper: Example migration note copy suggestion: "Historically some Dedicated clusters returned a direct `url` and numeric `id`. Hosted now returns `object_key` and string `id`; use the presign endpoint or SDK helper to obtain a downloadable URL. If you rely on numeric ids, convert to string-safe handling. Contact support for dedicated cluster mappings."

preview-bot: Preview for PR 1502 deployed: https://docs-preview.redwood.ai/pr/1502/upload-response-fix Please review the response schema and the migration note.

wayne: PR opened (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1502 Will add example changes + compatibility table. Assigning reviewers: elaine (docs), sanjay (tech), harper (QA).

elaine: Quick sanity-check from preview: examples render fine. Two nits: 1) add a tiny code snippet showing how to call presign endpoint with client.upload.presign(object_key) 2) call out that size_bytes is optional in legacy responses.

sanjay: I'll review wording for accuracy on legacy dedicated behaviour. Also confirm whether object_key is namespaced with customer id — yes it is, call that out.

harper: Added those edits to the PR branch. Will run SDK tests once merged. Thanks folks. :thumbsup:
